                                V2 LANDOWNERS’ REPLY BRIEF

        COMES NOW, Intervenors, CCD Properties Number 1, LLC (Party 744); Donna Baker

(Party 545); 760 County Road 350, LLC (Party 743); The Gibbons Ranch Limited Partnership

(Party 745); Daniel G. Rauh (Party 745); and Sloan Sisters Homestead, LP (Party 546)

(collectively, “V2 Landowners”) and timely file this their Reply Brief, and in support thereof

respectfully shows:

                                         I.        INTRODUCTION

        1.      V2 Landowners remain adamantly opposed to this 765-kV electric transmission

line being routed through any part of the pristine Texas Hill Country. Construction of any 765-kV

electric transmission line will have a profound and negative impact on the Texas Hill Country.

However, V2 Landowners reluctantly continue their support of Applicants’ “best meets” route,

route 894. Alternatively, V2 Landowners continue their support of the PUC Staff’s recommended

route, route 487, which closely follows route 894, with the exception of slight deviations. Finally,

should the ALJs fail to recommend routes 894 and 487, V2 Landowners would support route 296,

what has been designated as route CCG, route 392, route 410, route 416, or route 572.

                               II.     ARGUMENTS AND AUTHORITIES

        2.      After reviewing the Initial Briefs filed in this matter, V2 Landowners can find no

argument which conclusively shows that route 894 fails to best meet the criteria set forth in Public

Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA") § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B); is not forward

progressing; and is not constructible. After the Hearing on the Merits, Applicants have not put

forth any other specific route to replace route 894 as the “best meets” route. 1 Route 894 status as

the “best meets” route is further shown in the number of Intervenors who support and acknowledge

route 894 as the “best meets” route. 2 The Administrative Law Judges (“ALJs”) should recommend

route 894 to the PUC for approval.

        3.      Alternatively, the PUC continues to recommend route 487. 3 V2 Landowners can

find no argument in the Initial Briefs in this matter which conclusively shows that route 487 fails

to meet the criteria set forth in PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B); is not forward

progressing; and is not constructible. The PUC’s recommend route also has support from a number

of Intervenors. 4 Should the ALJs not recommend route 894, then route 487 should be

recommended to the PUC for approval.

        4.      A number of Intervenors have shown support for routes other than routes 894 and

487. Particularly, a number of Intervenors support route 572, 5 route 296, 6 what has been designated

                                           III.      CONCLUSION

        5.      V2 Landowners continue to support Applicants’ “best meets” route, route 894.

Alternatively, V2 Landowners continue to support the PUC Staff’s recommended route, route 487,

which closely follows route 894, with the exception of slight deviations. However, should the ALJs

fail to recommend routes 894 or 487, V2 Landowners would support route 296, what has been

designated as route CCG, route 392, route 410, route 416, or route 572.

                                               IV.    PRAYER

        WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, V2 Landowners respectfully request that the

ALJs recommend route 894 to the PUC for approval; alternatively, should the ALJs not

route 392, route 410, route 416, or route 572, should be recommended to the PUC for approval,

and for such further relief to which Intervenors may be entitled.
